CatchUp.fromSeconds is REQUIRED, not optional — advanceOver and solveCrossingOver must resume a partially consumed absence without restarting the warp. A crossing is a phase boundary, discovered rather than scheduled; re-entering with a fresh span pays for K absences instead of one, and each restart is cheaper, so the exploit climbs back in through the function that closes it.

OfflineCurve.uncappedSeconds documented as a design constraint: if a standing charge accrues on a cycle, U must exceed that cycle period by a wide margin or the cycle is skippable. The designer meets this at the field they are picking a number for.
tasks.notes: From D2. Also: the demo picked exponent 0.625 rather than 0.6 because 5/8 is dyadic, making credited time Tier A via a sqrt chain instead of pow. Check whether the default curve should do the same.

tasks.title: The landing page — a live argument, not a brochure
acceptance: NOTHING on the page is a picture of Lattice. Everything is Lattice, running — no screenshots, no video, no watch-the-demo button
the hero is a live isometric world rendering the moment the page paints, playable rather than merely animated: drag to pan, scroll to zoom, tap something and it responds
the gallery is fourteen LIVE scenes in a grid, not fourteen thumbnails — fourteen worlds animating at once in a page lighter than one hero image is a claim no competitor can make
chrome minimal, content maximal: IBM Plex Mono, near-black, almost no ornament — the type gets out of the way so the product is the only loud object
proof as numbers rather than adjectives: zero dependencies, zero assets, nine packages, ~78 kB gzipped, ~2,300 tests, and the live frame time shown on the page
the agent story is prominent and early — install the skills, point an agent at it, get a game. Show the actual invocation and what it produces
fast on a mid-range phone: tiles paused until scrolled into view, hero at a lower cadence off-screen. A page selling frame-time discipline cannot stutter
every tile links to its source, because a visitor who likes a tile wants the file immediately
tasks.notes: If the hero is static for even a second on load it reads as an image and the whole premise is lost. The page should hold itself to the zero-asset rule wherever it can even though it is exempt — a landing page that quietly needs a sprite sheet to look good is an argument against its own product.

sound is on the critical path, not decoration: the pitch relationships must actually be correct
voices stack without clipping when a player mashes every string at once, which is the first thing anyone does
the bed ducks under the puzzle tones and comes back — the one thing a sound board never asks of a mixer
lit only by the gates you have opened, so it earns the light field too
under 250 lines, most of it art; seed comes from the URL
tasks.notes: Exists because Instrument shows the synthesis but does not prove anyone would use it. You cannot fake this one.

install from npm pack tarballs, not the workspace: that exercises the files list, the exports map, the built dist and the shipped README, and catches the classic works-in-monorepo failure no test inside the monorepo can see
the session gets NO access to this repository; if it needs something only found here, that is the finding
judge it on the game, not the transcript — run it, look at it, screenshot it. Plausible code and a black screen is a failure, and this project has already made that exact mistake once
report in order: do the packages work outside the workspace, do the skills fire unasked, does an agent that never saw the RFCs avoid the traps anyway, and is the thing it built any good
tasks.notes: This is the last task. Anything it cannot do is the real backlog; everything before it is preparation.

tasks.title: Elevation across the iso/draw seam — three findings, one fix
acceptance: a terrain primitive that takes a tile whose four corners are at four different heights — draw has a Terrain PASS and no primitive that fits it, so every heightfield exhibit writes its own
zPx on drawSprite, SpriteDef massing, Animator and Emitter: on a heightfield every sprite floats or sinks, and the exhibit smuggled ground height through Variant.level as a documented abuse
zPx on SolidWriter.shadow and contactShadow — a building on a hill currently casts its shadow at sea level
pxToLevels to pair with levelsToPx: every elevation iso produces is world pixels and every height a sprite author writes is storeys, so  appears at every boundary in game code
a contract test above iso and draw — both have full coverage and no shared test, which is exactly how this got shipped
tasks.notes: The single largest gap the exhibit found. Findings 1, 2 and 11 are one fix.

tasks.title: Framing: camera.fitBounds, and a terrain cull the game can margin
acceptance: camera.fitBounds(rect, marginPx) — zoomAt takes a FACTOR and a required anchor, which is right for gestures and wrong for framing, and framing a generated world is the first thing every example does
renderFrame calls visibleTileBounds with no marginTiles, so a 440px summit vanished the moment its base left the screen — expose FrameOpts.maxHeightPx or a margin on Passes.terrain
the one place draw takes ownership from the game is the one place the game had the number
tasks.notes: Findings 3 and 9.

tasks.title: Decide who owns the drawable bucket
acceptance: DepthSorter deliberately cannot name a drawable, and both packages argued that split well — but the consequence is ~37 lines of index-aligned array in every game
a misalignment is a silent mis-pick, which is precisely the bug class pickSorted exists to prevent
decide: an optional item channel on DepthSorter, a shared helper in examples/_shared, or a documented refusal — but ten exhibits writing it ten times is not an answer
tasks.notes: Finding 6. The design was right and the ergonomics are wrong; those can both be true.

tasks.title: pathSimplify must not discard the weighted route
acceptance: its shortcut test is passability, not cost, so an A* result computed over a weighted cost function is straightened back into the straight line the weights existed to avoid
weighted pathfinding is iso.path headline feature and the only simplifier in the kit undoes it
the exhibit worked around it by passing a DIFFERENT predicate than its cost function, which nobody should have to discover
tasks.notes: Finding 5.

tasks.title: Small sharp edges the exhibit hit
acceptance: a failed PathFinder.find leaves an empty Path and pathSample/pathProject throw on one — correct per docs, and it is a white screen at boot the first time a seed puts a river across a gate
isoWall between two points differing equally in gx and gy has ZERO screen width, silently: world x is (gx-gy)*32. Prayer flags were invisible for a full iteration with nothing saying why

Vite HMR re-evaluates the module, createInput correctly throws on the double bind, and the FIRST instance keeps rendering — a zombie game with a frozen HUD. One line in input README saves every example an hour
wallText is hidden by its own roof overhang in the exhibit — either the overhang or the text needs to know about the other
tasks.notes: Findings 8, 10, 13b, and one drawing finding.

tasks.title: An idle economy headline rate is not expressible in sim graph
acceptance: edges are d(to)/dt += per x stock(from). The exhibit rate is pilgrims(reach) x k x sqrt(reach) — not linear in anything the graph holds
the whole rate went through one edge EdgeScale and was divided back out per lamp with a guard; it works, stays Tier A, and the division is the tell
decide whether the linear-producer shape is the right constraint and the docs should say so loudly, or whether a non-linear edge belongs in the surface
tasks.notes: Finding 7. EdgeScale is the sanctioned hook, so this may be a docs answer rather than an API one.

tasks.title: Palette needs game-defined slots
acceptance: Palette.lerp requires both stop sets to define exactly the same slots, which is right — but there is no way to add a GAME slot that participates in the lerp without redefining all three sets
the exhibit sand had to live outside the palette entirely, so it does not roll at dusk with everything else
tasks.notes: Finding 13.

tasks.title: Retire the demo RFC and tidy the exhibit
acceptance: docs/rfc/demo.md describes a game that no longer exists — offline accrual, presses, rockfall, the shrine ending. Retire it or re-scope it against docs/GALLERY.md
examples/demo/package.json declares @lattice/persist and @lattice/ui, neither imported

record what the exhibit cut left with NO consumer at all — persist entirely, sim.offline and sim.schedule in full including the CatchUp.fromSeconds that D2 added and nothing now calls, the whole replay story, FlowField, ChunkGrid, anchor
tasks.notes: The unused-feature list is the more important half: those are shipped features with zero real usage.

tasks.title: sim needs a source edge
acceptance: EdgeSpec.from becomes optional — there is currently no way to say "this rate multiplies nothing"

the exhibit added a node to its economy purely to be a multiplicand it then divided back out, and EconomySpec.nodes IS the save field order, so a save file carries a field because of a missing optional
with from? the demo economy drops to a single node — verify that against examples/demo

document that EdgeScale is evaluated once per buildFlow, so the real constraint is piecewise-constant IN TIME rather than linear: square-root and threshold rates were never excluded and the docs implied they were
tasks.notes: From docs/rfc/sim-rates.md. The division in the exhibit was a tell for this, not for non-linear rates.

tasks.title: Retrofit the exhibit HUD onto @lattice/ui
acceptance: the exhibit drew its HUD into the canvas because ui had not landed yet; ui is now built and has NO consumer anywhere in the gallery plan
number rolls instead of jumping values, a button with an affordable state, a toast — the things ui owed and canvas text cannot do well
exercise the paletteVars to CSS custom-property bridge: the overlay must darken with the world at dusk. This is the one cross-package promise nothing has ever executed
hud.ts already keeps a Hud interface as the seam — swap the body, keep the call
report honestly if ui made this harder than canvas text did; that is a finding about ui, not a reason to revert
tasks.notes: A whole package reached 100% coverage with no consumer in the entire plan. This is the fix.

tasks.title: Decide whether iso.ChunkGrid ships at all
acceptance: flagged as a DELETE candidate rather than a coverage gap: no plausible consumer, and every planned exhibit fits one viewport
the alternative to deleting is naming the game shape that needs it and adding an exhibit that is that shape
a feature with no consumer and no planned consumer is surface we maintain forever for nobody — decide, and write the reason down either way
tasks.notes: Also fix draw/src/index.ts, whose comment justifies keeping record.ts on the grounds that ui wants it for layout measurement. Nothing in ui references the recording surface.

tasks.title: input must be told an overlay is legitimate
acceptance: covered-by-overlay fires on the FIRST TAP on any HUD over the canvas — including every @lattice/ui panel
this now BLOCKS a rule: GALLERY.md requires exhibits use ui for their overlay, so every exhibit would hit it
the bootstrap works around it by filtering on class name, which is exactly the kind of workaround a kit exists to remove
wants InputOptions.overlays, or something better — decide the shape
tasks.notes: Blocking. Discovered by the gallery bootstrap, one commit after ui was made the mandatory overlay.

tasks.title: createInput.stepMs should not take a bare number
acceptance: it takes a bare number and rejects only 0 and NaN, so stepMs:16 against a 16.667ms loop is a long press at 432ms, a fling 4% low, and a log persist refuses months later

CORRECTED AFTER THE FACT: this criterion originally claimed core has a branded duration type that would stop the substitution. It does not — see docs/rfc/durations.md. A brand separates kinds and a duration has only one kind. What shipped is the right answer: take the loop itself, structurally, and cross-check the two fields it publishes.
also: no input.setProfile, so retuning one threshold means dispose, recreate, and re-register every handler
tasks.notes: The acceptance list above contains one criterion I wrote that was false, corrected in place rather than deleted, because a wrong claim left in a done task is prior art the next agent will find.

tasks.title: Camera cannot read back its own policy
acceptance: minZoom, maxZoom and keepVisible go in at construction and vanish — there is no reader and no setZoomLimits
the gallery panel had to keep a shadow copy and rebuild the camera AND the input on every drag of a zoom slider
a value a caller supplied and cannot read back is a value they must store twice, and two copies drift

tasks.title: Options as data per call, not closed at construction
acceptance: sim passes its parameters per call, so every one of its knobs is live; every other package closes its options over at construction
that single difference is what forced a rebuild-on-change path into the gallery control panel

audio is the sharp case: mixer is mutable post-construction, the voice ceiling is not, and dispose() closes the AudioContext — a document gets about six, so a live voice slider can PERMANENTLY SILENCE THE PAGE
draw is the arbitrary case: falloff is per-call on add, while scale and bloom are construction-only, with no principle separating them
decide whether this is a kit-wide rule worth stating in AGENTS.md, or a per-package judgement — but the asymmetry should be deliberate rather than accidental
tasks.notes: The most interesting observation from the gallery bootstrap. It is an architecture question, not a bug.

tasks.title: Delete the exhibit workarounds, and fix the picking bug they were hiding
acceptance: LIVE BUG FIRST: spriteVolume is called without the ground, so a silhouette is computed at sea level while the building is painted up the hill — taps on tall-standing lamps land in mid-air, partly masked by a hand-written bubble fallback
delete terrainQuad and its helpers for draw.isoTerrain — AND FLIP THE RELIEF SIGN, the exhibit shades west-minus-east and the kit ships the corrected east-minus-west
delete zOf and the Variant.level smuggling: six massings, five animators, three emitters, and the level computed in push()
delete the grow re-margin in the terrain pass for Passes.maxHeightPx
move SAND into the palette via extendStops so the beach rolls at dusk with everything else
adopt the shared bootstrap and Bucket from examples/_shared
report the new logic-to-art line split — the whole point of these fixes is that logic should shrink
tasks.notes: Every item here was a workaround the kit forced, and one of them turned out to be a real bug. That is the argument for extracting workarounds rather than admiring them.

tasks.title: isoWall should refuse an edge-on wall rather than draw nothing
acceptance: iso now exports isEdgeOn — the predicate for a wall whose two points have equal gx and gy deltas, which projects to a vertical line and draws zero pixels
isoWall should assert on it in dev, or refuse and name the two tiles. iso cannot warn: it has no console and no dev/prod distinction, so this is draw side
the exhibit lost a full iteration to invisible prayer flags with nothing anywhere saying why
tasks.notes: Routed from iso.

tasks.title: audio.maxVoices and maxPan must be live
acceptance: GALLERY.md REQUIRES a voice-ceiling slider, and the current shape means that slider can permanently silence the page: dispose() closes the AudioContext and a document gets about six
maxVoices is one integer in a comparison — no allocation, no handle to invalidate, nothing downstream with a correctness claim that it did not change
add the readers too, per the new eleventh non-negotiable
tasks.notes: The sharpest row in docs/rfc/live-options.md.

tasks.title: draw.LightField.configure is write-only
acceptance: configure() landed hours ago and shipped HALF the pair — there are no scale/bloom/falloff getters, so a panel showing current bloom beside its slider still keeps a shadow copy
this is the strongest single piece of evidence for the readback rule: mutability is the interesting half and gets thought about, readback costs three lines and gets skipped

also fix the record.ts comment in draw/src/index.ts — it claims ui wants the recording surface for layout measurement, and nothing in ui references it. The real justification is a PLANNED consumer, the Replay exhibit, and the replacement text must say planned rather than reading as already-true

tasks.title: input.setProfile and setActions must both refuse during a recording
acceptance: setProfile refusing while a recording is open is the right shape — system.ts:639 already uses those words four lines away

BUT the RFC author found a hole in their own recommendation: making actions live is NOT covered by that refusal. The log stores RawSamples and actions is not in the compatibility triple, so a mid-recording rebind silently changes what a replay DOES with a triple that still matches
either setActions refuses too, or actions joins the triple — decide and say why
tasks.notes: Self-caught by the RFC author. A recommendation that finds its own hole is worth more than one that does not.

tasks.title: Two packages are over the size budget
acceptance: draw is 12.74 kB against 12; input is 13.88 against its documented 13 kB override
this is a real gate failure on committed code, not a rounding issue — decide per package: trim, or raise the override with a written reason
iso frees 0.64 kB when ChunkGrid is deleted, which is more than its entire remaining headroom — that is the shape of the argument to apply here
do NOT raise the global. A limit that moves outward whenever something exceeds it is not a limit

tasks.title: Delete iso.ChunkGrid
acceptance: docs/rfc/chunkgrid.md has an 11-step deletion checklist — follow it, including invariants.test.ts expect(checked).toBe(56) becoming 54
the three doc comments in path.ts and height.ts must be REWORDED to name tileSourceOf, not deleted, or PathOptions.maxNodes loses its stated justification and the next author raises it
0.64 kB gzipped against iso having 0.45 kB of headroom — it is larger than everything iso has left, spent on the only module with no reader
record the revisit trigger: a second WRITER, not a bigger map. A bigger map is new TileGrid(512,512); endless procedural terrain is tileSourceOf and free

tasks.title: The kit has no branded duration type, and two briefs assumed it did
acceptance: core exports EpochMillis and MonotonicMillis, both branded — but neither is a DURATION. Millis belongs to @lattice/loop, is a bare number alias, and its own doc comment says it guards nothing
so a { stepMs: Millis } parameter was never an available shape for a sibling package, and the acceptance criterion I wrote for K13 asserted that it was
a brand living in loop cannot help any sibling across the DAG. input took the step STRUCTURALLY instead, as the two fields the loop already publishes, and cross-checks them
decide whether a branded duration belongs in core, or whether structural pairs are the better answer kit-wide — input argues a cross-checked pair is self-verifying in a way a brand is not
audit how many other briefs and RFCs assume a duration brand exists
tasks.notes: Found by a builder while implementing a criterion I wrote that was false. The interesting question is how many other places carry the same assumption.

tasks.title: examples/_shared/bucket.ts was specified and never built
acceptance: docs/rfc/depth-bucket.md specifies it and assigns it to G0. G0 shipped the bootstrap and the panel without it

the exhibit applied the named PATTERN by hand — one array, one index space, the subtraction gone — but the add-time index compare that makes the silent mis-pick unreachable is the helper and it does not exist
that compare is the entire reason the RFC chose a helper over a documented pattern: a pattern is followed until someone is in a hurry
fourteen exhibits are about to be written against it
tasks.notes: The one acceptance item on the exhibit cleanup that could not be met. A specified deliverable that quietly did not ship is worth more attention than a bug.

tasks.title: Lamp Road is 1,286 lines against the gallery rule of 250
acceptance: the rule postdates this exhibit, so the question is which is wrong — the exhibit or the rule
the split is 295 logic / 1,095 art, and art is what the rule was meant to encourage, so a raw line cap may be measuring the wrong thing
either cut the exhibit to the rule, or change the rule to bound LOGIC and let art run — and say which in GALLERY.md
whatever is decided binds the other thirteen exhibits, so decide before they are written rather than after
tasks.notes: Flagged by the exhibit author as the largest single thing wrong with it as a gallery row.

tasks.title: Delete the Millis and Seconds aliases from loop
acceptance: these are bare number aliases whose own doc says they guard nothing, and they are the VECTOR for a false claim that a branded duration exists

kit.json lists them among loop exports alphabetized beside Loop and Scheduler, one package away from core EpochMillis, with nothing distinguishing a type that guards from a synonym for number — and agents read the manifest first, because AGENTS.md tells them to
36 type positions; every use site field name already ends in Ms or Seconds, so the deletion is mechanical
this is the actual cause and the cheapest fix in the set
tasks.notes: The prose was never the failure — four documents stated the truth, two of them in the source of the packages involved, and the false claim was written twice anyway.

tasks.title: tools/gallery.mjs — enforce the logic cap the rule now states
acceptance: print each exhibit logic/art split and fail the one over 200 logic code lines

classification is per MODULE via an @art tag in the header doc comment, per GALLERY.md — a module is art if deleting it changes only what the exhibit looks or sounds like, holds no state past a frame, and moves no number the player is playing for
ambiguity resolves to logic. Until this tool exists the grep in GALLERY.md is the rule, which means the rule is currently unenforced
also worth a lint rule for the one lintable piece: every duration parameter name ends in Ms or Seconds, which catches the after(3000)-means-fifty-minutes class

tasks.title: DepthSorter needs a sorted flag — it is the only thing blocking a whole invariant
acceptance: the shared Bucket cannot meet its invariant B7 — "an unsorted each throws" — from outside the package, and the reason is worth reading: DepthSorter publishes nothing that separates "not sorted" from "sorted, nothing culled"

pre-sort, count equals the bucket count and indexAt(i) === i — and an unculled frame filled in depth order is BIT-IDENTICAL to that. Any detector built on the published surface is a false alarm on a real frame
a public `sorted` flag, lowered by add and clear and raised by sort, is three lines and unblocks it
the bucket test already asserts the gap as a tripwire, so whoever adds the flag is told where to come back
tasks.notes: A helper outside the package could not close it, and said so rather than shipping a detector that would cry wolf. That is the right call and it routes here.

tasks.title: The waypost flag can reach isoWall's new refusal
acceptance: the flag animates sway into BOTH coordinates in proportion, which is edge-on exactly when sway is 0 — and isoWall now throws rather than silently drawing nothing

it does not fire today, and the check for that was thorough: core noise2 returns exactly 0 at 397k of 14M lattice samples, but only when BOTH inputs are lattice points, and the phase here is fractional — 0 exact zeros in 200k samples
move the sway onto one axis rather than relying on a fractional phase nobody will remember is load-bearing
two neighboring sprites were checked and are safe by construction — their wave would have to reach 1.2 and 0.52 against ranges of 0.12 and 0.17
tasks.notes: The one shape in the repo that can reach the new throw. Safe by accident is not safe.

tasks.title: The size tool sums two backends no consumer ships together
acceptance: draw is the only package with two mutually exclusive backends: a browser game ships canvas2d and not record, a headless replay ships record and not canvas2d
the gate reads their sum, which is a bundle nobody downloads — 12.93 against a real 12.08 or 11.30

this is the same species as the adapter finding already fixed, but the fix is different: an adapter IS downloaded by a game and must stay counted, whereas mutually exclusive backends genuinely cannot both ship
decide whether the tool should report a per-entry-point figure, and note that getting this right retires draw's override rather than merely explaining it
